verified.catalyst: The FTC decides whether to sue to block, settle with divestitures, or let the Cintas deal ($155 cash + 0.772 CTAS per share) close; the parties' agreed no-close date is Dec 11, 2026, and Cintas still guides to close before year-end.
verified.dated_milestone: Dec 11, 2026: timing agreement expires, so expect an FTC vote and complaint, or a consent decree, around then. Next: if the FTC sues, a PI/Part 3 schedule in early 2026-27, with the outside date running about 10 months plus extensions from Mar 2026.
verified.instrument: UNF common, ideally hedged by shorting 0.772 CTAS per UNF share to lock the stock leg. Unhedged, it carries CTAS beta on about 52% of the consideration.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 named counterparty (Cintas, signed merger agreement, shareholder-approved Jun 2026). G2 concrete commitment ($155.00 cash + 0.7720 CTAS per share; $350M antitrust reverse termination fee). G3 specific unpriced figure: a 40.6% gross spread ($324.01 implied vs $230.40), which prices only about 25-30% odds of closing.
verified.edge: M. The spread pays about 3:1 (+$94 if it closes vs about -$30 if blocked), but whether the FTC sues or accepts a remedy can't be known in advance, and it is a contested litigation binary. Residual capture: (a) run-up from the pre-catalyst base (about $168, the 90-day average before Cintas went public with its Dec 2025 offer, implied by the 64% premium on $275) to $230.40 is about +37%, and most of that gain was given back after the Oct 27 FTC leak; (b) remaining to the favorable resolution value of $324.01 (at CTAS $218.92) is +40.6%. The event is not harvested: the market is pricing a block, not the close. Downside floor about $195-200, which is standalone value near the pre-deal base plus about $19/sh of fee. That floor is soft because an FTC suit alone does not trigger the fee; it pays only on termination on antitrust grounds.
verified.primary_source: FMP batch-quote 2026-11-20 (UNF $230.40, CTAS $218.92); Semafor/Reuters via Investing.com and TIKR, 2026-10-27 (FTC intends to sue, not yet voted); MLex 2026 (parties agree not to close before Dec 11 unless the FTC closes its probe); Cintas/UniFirst merger announcement, Barchart, Mar 2026 ($155 + 0.7720 CTAS, $5.5B EV); UniFirst Form 425 on SEC EDGAR.
verified.kill_fact: Prices check out: FMP live quote on 2026-11-20 has UNF at $230.40 (-$10.82, -4.5%) and CTAS at $218.92. The deal is worth $155 + 0.772 x $218.92 = $324.01, a gross spread of 40.6%. Semafor reported on Oct 27 that the FTC would sue; the FTC spokesperson said it has not voted; I found no complaint or remedy filed as of today. The no-close-before-Dec-11 date and the $350M reverse fee are confirmed, and the fee does not fire on a suit alone. Correction: today's drop is not clearly a new leak. UNF rose about 6.6% on Nov 18 (Zacks), so today mostly gives that back, and CTAS also fell 1.4%. That makes the drop in the deal-implied value larger than UNF's own move. Score cut: the event has not fired, but it is a binary FTC vote with staff already leaning to sue. A suit at or after Dec 11 does not trigger the fee and would tie up capital in litigation for 6-12 months. The floor rests on the pre-deal standalone price; the 52-week low is $159.82, so the real downside could be well below $198. Run it hedged only, and size it as a lottery-like binary, not as a 40% spread.
verified.analysis: The deal terms are verified: $155 cash + 0.772 CTAS, $310 at signing in Mar 2026, a $350M reverse fee on antitrust grounds, and no closing before Dec 11, 2026. FMP quote 2026-11-20: UNF $230.40 (-4.5%, -$10.82), CTAS $218.92, for a gross spread of about 40.6%. Semafor reported on Oct 27 that the FTC told Cintas it would sue; the FTC says it has not voted, and I found no complaint or remedy filing through today. I could not find the cause of today's -$10.82 drop (gap), so a fresh negative leak is possible. A cash/stock deal price is contractual, so the numerator provenance check is exempt. At a blended floor of about $198, the price implies roughly 25-30% odds of closing. That is cheap if a divestiture settlement is plausible (UNF+CTAS is a horizontal overlap, and the fix is likely regional route divestitures), and fair if the FTC litigates to a PI win. Score 6, not 7: the outcome depends on an agency vote with negative leaks and an unexplained drop today, the fee does not fire on a suit alone, and the downside path, a suit plus litigation, could tie up capital for 6-12 months.

verified.primary_source: Axcelis/Veeco joint press release 'Update on Expected Timing of Merger Closing', 2026-11-02 (finviz/webull, MLex 2026-11); Joint Proxy Statement/Prospectus, Jan 2026 (fixed 0.3575 ratio); FMP batch-quote, 2026-11-20
verified.analysis: The deal and the regulatory timeline are real. The 2026-11-02 joint release confirms SAMR is still pending, HSR has to be refiled, and closing is now expected by end-Q1 2027. But at today's quotes VECO trades about 4.9% above the 0.3575 x ACLS implied value, so a long VECO earns nothing if the deal closes. The inversion suggests the market is pricing VECO's standalone/break value, a short-ACLS borrow cost, or a quote anomaly, not a regulatory-risk discount. The stock-for-stock structure means no cash anchor. Treat this as WATCH only: re-check whether the spread turns positive (VECO below 0.3575 x ACLS) on SAMR headlines. Gaps: no outside date or termination fees verified from the primary merger agreement (a secondary summary cites $108.7M payable by ACLS and $77.5M payable by VECO), and one quote snapshot was not cross-checked intraday.
